The hepatitis A virus and the hepatitis C virus are differentiated by their type of genetic material, with hepatitis A having a single-stranded RNA genome and hepatitis C also having a single-stranded RNA genome. The methodology used for detection varies, with hepatitis A detected using serological tests and hepatitis C detected using molecular methods. The structure of the capsid and the presence or absence of a wrap around the capsid are not key factors in differentiating these viruses.
